sources.title: NGSS 5-LS2-1: Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment
OpenStax Biology 2e, 24.3 Ecology of Fungi (fungi as decomposers and recyclers)
OpenStax Biology 2e, 22.3 Prokaryotic Metabolism (bacteria and fungi are decomposers)
OpenStax Biology 2e, 44.3 Terrestrial Biomes (decaying leaf litter returns nutrients to the soil)

note.text: On the forest floor, dead leaves, logs and animals pile up. Something has to break them down.

steps.title: Tree
steps.instruction: Trace the tree's trunk and crown.

note.text: A tree builds its leaves and wood using air, water, and nutrients from the soil.
Roots take up water and nutrients from the soil.
Each fall, many trees drop their leaves. The leaves still hold nutrients the tree used.
Dead wood is matter too. Over years, it slowly rots away.

steps.title: Mushrooms
steps.instruction: Trace the two mushrooms on the log.

note.text: Mushrooms are fungi. Fungi break down dead plants and animals, freeing nutrients that other living things need.

steps.title: Bacteria
steps.instruction: Trace the five bacteria in the soil.

note.text: Bacteria are far too small to see; these are drawn huge. Along with fungi, they break down dead matter.

steps.title: The cycle
steps.instruction: Draw the arrows: leaves fall, nutrients go into the soil, roots take them up.

note.text: As dead leaves and wood decay, their nutrients return to the soil, where roots can take them up again.

steps.title: Recycling
items: Fungi and bacteria break them down
Nutrients go back into the soil
steps.why: Decomposers break down dead matter, returning its nutrients to the soil for plants to use again.
steps.hint: What happens first, in the fall?

steps.title: Predict
steps.instruction: Imagine a forest with no decomposers.
steps.question: What would happen in a forest with no fungi or bacteria?

options.text: Dead leaves and logs would pile up, and the soil would run short of nutrients
options.feedback: Yes. Without decomposers, nutrients stay locked in dead matter instead of returning to the soil for plants.
Trees need the nutrients decomposers return to the soil. Without them, the soil runs short.
Decomposers recycle nutrients. Without them, dead matter piles up and soil runs short.

options.text: Leaves would turn back into trees
options.feedback: Dead leaves can't do that. Decomposers break them down so their nutrients reach new plants.

steps.title: Classify
steps.question: Which of these is a decomposer?

options.text: A mushroom growing on a dead log
options.feedback: Right. Mushrooms are fungi, which break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil.
An oak is a producer: it makes its own food from sunlight.
A rabbit eats living plants, so it's a consumer, not a decomposer.
An owl hunts animals, so it's a consumer. Decomposers break down dead matter.
